overall_statistics.intro: The released benchmark split is carved out from a larger reviewed scene pool. The released statistics below describe the benchmark-facing subset, while the figure retains the paper-level overview of released scenes, landmarks, and task counts.

landmark_category.intro: Released landmarks cover eight coarse categories and a long-tailed set of fine-grained subcategories. The table lists the dominant coarse categories in the released split, while the dual-ring chart shows how those coarse categories expand into their constituent subcategories.

scene_coverage.intro: The selected benchmark split spans twelve scenes rather than collapsing around a single environment. The released split keeps landmark, image-task, and video-task contributions visible scene by scene.

task_distribution.intro: Task allocation is balanced first at the cognition level and then at the task-family level. The inner ring aggregates samples by the two cognition axes, while the outer ring expands them into the six released tasks.

image_branch.intro: Image tasks are built from landmark-centric multiview evidence. Each released landmark may contribute up to eight canonical orbit views, and Stage 4 additionally captures task-specific observation images such as the query views used by environment-aware tasks.
image_branch.gallery_intro: The selector below shows ten released landmarks that preserve the full eight-view coverage used by the image-task pipeline.

video_branch.intro: Video tasks are assembled from an explicit Stage 3 behavior library. Atomic modes define the primitive maneuvers, while composite modes chain those primitives into inspection-style missions that support both behavior recognition and visibility reasoning.
